reason: Frillish/Jellicent and Dragalge establish a haunted wreck, while 30% Super Rod Dhelmise makes its signature discovery practical.
Mareanie, Golisopod and Clawitzer give the flooded cabins a strong scavenger identity; Lapras is the generic outlier.
recommendation: Replace the 10% Surf Lapras slot with Barbaracle, retaining Lapras at its other coastal locations and Dhelmise in both wreck interiors.

reason: The coast has useful catches but no finale-specific reward, and its Super Rod roster exactly duplicates Route124.
recommendation: Use a waterfall Super Rod roster of Kingdra 30%, Barraskewda 25%, Gyarados 20%, Cloyster 15% and Relicanth 10%; promote the 35% Surf Wailmer slot to Wailord.

reason: The bird-filled bay, shore Rock Smash pool and several useful fishing families feel convincingly coastal.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Shellder at 25% with Cloyster so the strongest rod offers a ready evolved shellfish beside Kingler, while preserving Shellder elsewhere.

reason: Staryu/Starmie fit the star-associated city and give useful options, but generic Wailord leads its strongest rod.
recommendation: Exchange Super Rod Wailord and Starmie chances, making Starmie 30% and Wailord 10%; replace Good Rod Luvdisc at 25% with Staryu to establish the family across methods.

reason: Alomomola and seabirds make the floating town recognizable, but its Super Rod mostly repeats the surrounding ocean.
recommendation: Keep the town Surf roster; replace Super Rod Shellder 15% and Lapras 10% with Huntail and Gorebyss respectively to make shell-bed fishing beneath the town its discovery.

reason: Mantine and Clamperl define a useful shelf habitat, but the strongest rod is an interchangeable ocean pool.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Bruxish 30% with Mantine and Wailord 20% with Cloyster; retain the other fishing options and the entire separate Dive roster.

reason: Spheal, Dewgong and Walrein introduce Shoal beautifully, but warm-reef fishing species dilute that cold-current identity.
recommendation: Use Super Rod Qwilfish 30%, Cloyster 25%, Walrein 20%, Dewgong 15% and Hisuian Qwilfish 10%, replacing Luvdisc, Corsola and Dragalge in that method.

reason: Alomomola and Wishiwashi form a recognizable reef community, with Aqua Tauros and Feebas providing memorable useful catches.
recommendation: Keep Aqua Tauros and Feebas; replace Super Rod Kingler 25% with Wishiwashi and Shellder 20% with Gorebyss to better connect surface fishing to the shell-and-coral reef below.

reason: Mareanie/Toxapex and Pyukumuku make this a clear defensive reef, but its strongest rod returns to whales and generic shellfish.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Kingler 30% with Toxapex and Wailord 15% with Corsola, keeping the other methods and their readily available Bruxish.

reason: The cavern approach offers strong marine partners, but Wailmer-led Surf overlaps heavily with Route129 and nearby cities.
recommendation: Make Surf Sharpedo 35%, Jellicent 25%, Malamar 18%, Alomomola 12% and Finizen 10%; replace Super Rod Lapras 10% with Jellicent for a predator-and-ghost approach to Seafloor Cavern.

reason: The Wailmer/Wailord population makes a good whale route, but the leading Super Rod catch does not support that identity.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Hisuian Qwilfish 30% with Wailord, Relicanth 15% with Mantine and Basculegion 10% with Finizen; keep Basculegion concentrated in the ghost-water locations.

reason: The 43% Wynaut colony makes Mirage Island distinctive, and Frillish/Jellicent give its water a theme; the rods still repeat adjacent routes.
recommendation: Preserve the complete Wynaut land colony; replace Super Rod Hisuian Qwilfish 30% with Jellicent, Qwilfish 20% with Octillery and Relicanth 15% with Wishiwashi, retaining Basculegion 10% as the ghost-water reward.

reason: Relicanth on Surf and Old Rod suits the ancient-pillar approach, but its Super Rod pool exactly duplicates Route134.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Octillery 25% with Relicanth, Seadra 20% with Kingdra and Basculegion 10% with Gyarados, tying the stronger rod to ancient marine and dragon discoveries.

reason: Carvanha, Barraskewda and Old Rod Arrokuda suit the rushing current, but common Surf Magikarp and the deep-relic rod pool weaken that theme.
recommendation: Replace Surf Magikarp 25% with Sharpedo; use Super Rod Barraskewda 30%, Sharpedo 25%, Mantine 20%, Clawitzer 15% and Finizen 10% for the fast open-water channel.

reason: Spheal-led Surf mixes cold-water, reef and current identities, while the rods provide little distinction from neighboring sea routes.
recommendation: Make Surf Mantine 35%, Pelipper 25%, Dragalge 18%, Cramorant 12% and Finizen 10%; use Super Rod Bruxish 30%, Octillery 25%, Lanturn 20%, Clawitzer 15% and Kingdra 10% for a bird-and-reef eddy between the fast channel and relic shallows.

reason: Huntail/Gorebyss suggest good shell beds, but Seel leads Surf and the Super Rod is identical to Route131.
recommendation: Replace Surf Seel 35% with Relicanth; use Super Rod Relicanth 30%, Huntail 25%, Gorebyss 20%, Clawitzer 15% and Gyarados 10% to make the Sealed Chamber approach a fossil-and-shell habitat.

reason: Tropical forms, big herbivores and strong insects form a rich reserve with useful catches and a complementary rocky excavation pool.
The herd species are useful, but bugs, Houndour and repeated reserve residents leave the zone less distinctive than its neighbors.
recommendation: Replace land Houndour 13%, Pineco 12% and Forretress 11% with Miltank, Tauros and Stantler respectively, yielding herds at 23%, 22% and 17%; emphasize the two bugs in Southeast instead and keep the current Rock Smash pool.

reason: Birds, rhinos, Kangaskhan and Chansey make an excellent safari grassland, but its Good Rod ignores the surrounding freshwater habitat.
recommendation: Replace Good Rod Lanturn 45%, Sharpedo 30% and Octillery 25% with Quagsire, Whiscash and Golduck respectively; retain the land roster and both Dratini methods.

reason: Regional cats, Raichu, Wobbuffet, Smeargle, Chansey and Ditto make a distinct specialist-support collection with practical encounter chances.
Gligar, Flaaffy and woodland mammals are useful, but substantial Johto overlap and generic fishing blur the zone.
recommendation: Replace land Stantler 8% and Quagsire 7% with Pineco and Forretress; keep Quagsire on Super Rod, replace Good Rod Octillery 30% with Poliwhirl, and replace Super Rod Sharpedo 25% with Crawdaunt.

reason: Wetland bugs, frogs and the complete Goomy line form a coherent habitat with both developing and immediately evolved choices; the ponds support it.
Good Rod Relicanth and Dragalge provide a useful deep-water welcome, but Surf Magikarp and the repeated pufferfish rod pool feel generic.
recommendation: Replace Surf Magikarp 12% with Lanturn; replace Super Rod Hisuian Qwilfish 30% with Relicanth and Qwilfish 25% with Kingdra, retaining Octillery, Seadra and Basculegion.

reason: A 34% Dragalge population with Golisopod gives the first chamber a strong identity and useful immediate partners.
recommendation: Merge Barraskewda 8% into Grapploct, making it 15%, and Sharpedo 5% into Toxapex, making it 15%; those displaced species remain in other cavern rooms.

reason: Sharpedo and Basculegion have promise, but eleven species still resemble a broad mixture of the surrounding chambers.
recommendation: Merge Kingdra 5% and Dragalge 7% into Sharpedo, making its resident population 33%; keep the bats, Floatzel, Basculegion and remaining shoreline partners.

reason: Dhelmise at 29% beside Claydol, Sableye and Bronzong makes a distinctive submerged-relic chamber with useful team-building roles.
Malamar gives the room a possible identity, but most slots repeat the general cavern pool and differ little from Room2.
recommendation: Merge Sharpedo 13% into Malamar for 32%, Barraskewda 8% into Bruxish for 13%, and Golisopod 10% into Grapploct for 15%, emphasizing strange psychic predators and grapplers.

reason: Kingdra at 34% is a clear payoff, though Golisopod still takes a large repeated share beside the dragon residents.
recommendation: Merge the Golisopod 22% slots into Kingdra, making a 56% Kingdra colony with Dragalge at 16% and the remaining five supporting species unchanged.

reason: Barbaracle distinguishes land, but the Surf and rod pools largely replay ghosts and predators already caught elsewhere.
recommendation: Merge land Dragalge 12% and Kingdra 5% into Barbaracle for 40%; change Surf Frillish 35% to Binacle, Jellicent 18% to Golisopod and Lapras 10% to Clawitzer; change Super Rod Dragalge 25% to Barbaracle and Basculegion 10% to Grapploct.

reason: The Toxapex shore and Huntail/Gorebyss water can be distinctive, but land overlap and generic fishing obscure those strengths.
recommendation: Merge land Malamar 10% and Kingdra 5% into Toxapex for 38%; change Good Rod Luvdisc 30% to Clamperl; use Super Rod Huntail 30%, Gorebyss 25%, Toxapex 20%, Clamperl 15% and Relicanth 10%.

reason: The compact evolved roster is strong, but Kingdra/Dragalge repeat Room5 and unique Clobbopus is only a small discovery.
recommendation: Keep Clobbopus 5%; replace Kingdra 23% with Grapploct and merge Dragalge 23% into Basculegion for 28%, retaining Golisopod, Clawitzer and Crobat as the deep-chamber supporting cast.

reason: The cold coast offers good choices, but twelve land species blur the deeper rooms and Surf Snom plus rod Cetoddle are awkward placements.
recommendation: Merge land Zubat 13% into Spheal for 25%; replace Surf Snom 12% with Lapras and Cetoddle 10% with Eiscue; replace Super Rod Cetoddle 10% with Cloyster, preserving Snom and Cetoddle in the cave land rosters.

reason: Alolan Vulpix, Iron Bundle, Arctibax and regional forms make a memorable ice-room payoff, with strong snow-team options and sensible encounter chances.
Galarian Darumaka is an excellent find, but ten of twelve land species match the stairs and Cetoddle again occupies water and rod slots.
recommendation: Merge land Spheal 12% and Bergmite 8% into Galarian Darumaka for 33%, and replace Snom 6% with land Cetoddle; replace Surf Cetoddle 35% with Sealeo, Super Rod Cetoddle 10% with Cloyster and Luvdisc 25% with Lapras.

reason: Alolan Sandshrew is a worthwhile exclusive, but almost everything around it repeats the neighboring cold rooms.
recommendation: Merge land Spheal 12% and Snover 8% into Alolan Sandshrew for 33%, then replace Cubchoo 7% with Alolan Sandslash for an armored-ice colony; retain the remaining residents.

reason: The roster has no distinct signature and shares ten of twelve species with the inner room, despite its useful individual catches.
recommendation: Merge Spheal 13% into Swinub for 24%, Seel 12% into Bergmite for 20%, and Snorunt 10% into Cubchoo for 17%; replace Snom 5% with Piloswine to create a recognizable burrowing-ice transition.

reason: Clauncher, Skrelp, Kingler and Dhelmise fit a busy port and make returning with better rods worthwhile.
recommendation: Replace Super Rod Clamperl 30% with Clawitzer and Seadra 20% with Starmie, connecting the advanced rod to the port families available through the earlier rods; retain Dhelmise 10%.

reason: Alomomola and schooling fish suit the sheltered crater, but its fishing barely develops the existing Gyarados landmark identity.
recommendation: Reorder Surf to Gyarados 35%, Alomomola 25%, Wishiwashi 18%, Finizen 12% and Clamperl 10%; replace Super Rod Kingler 20% with Milotic and Qwilfish 15% with Gyarados, preserving the Dive reef unchanged.

reason: Lanturn, Starmie, Dondozo and deep predators make Dive immediately rewarding, with broad useful roles and distinct uncommon finds.
Coral and shellfish lead naturally into Cursola, Milotic and Palafin, giving the reef a coherent identity and worthwhile Dive discoveries.
Dondozo and all three Tatsugiri forms make the submarine habitat a memorable doubles-team discovery, supported by rare deep-sea surprises.
